closeReason: Stale (consultant review, relayed 09:56 CST Nov 17): PR 3542 was reverted by PR 3555, and PR 3592 voids the question.
context:
Goal: a lane's lint result means what CI means, and settings.json and its test agree.
Problem (rule): main's commit a8c3af717e (PR #3542, allow-merge-ready, merged 19:51Z = 13:51 CST) added two allow rules to the root settings.json: "Bash(~/.claude/bin/merge --ready *)" and "Bash(verdict ~/.claude/bin/merge --ready *)". The test merge/test_merge.py::CloudAllow::test_the_repo_settings_json_has_no_merge_allow_rule (line ~14820) says no allow rule may contain "bin/merge". Replaying its asserts against main's settings.json gives 2 failures; the parent commit gives 0. No decision or ruling records the allow rule; PR #3542's body says only "The owner asked for the allow rule in chat". The checks-windows-merge job failed on PR #3542's head; its log was not read. Needs your word: is the test stale, or does the allow rule go?
Based on (measured): the read-only replay of the test's asserts against origin/main; the full test run is unmeasured.
Departs from: main — the test says no merge allow rule; main's settings.json now has one.
If you did not ask for this rule, pick b.
Update 15:22 CST: main is red because of #3542 (push run 43754746334 on c47fe6003): checks-merge-git, checks-windows-merge (shard 1 of 5) and checks-install-checkout all fail on the two new allow rules; the same three failed on the PR's own head run. The consultant (relayed, not owner-typed) reverts #3542 now under the red-main rule and has the lane re-land the allow rule with the test fixed, so option a is what is under way and option b (rule removed) is what the revert does until the re-land. This item stays open for your answer on whether the allow rule should exist at all; the PR body says you asked for it in chat.
holds: PR #3551 waits on this answer (the lane waits; the PR stays draft).

options.gain: Your chat ask stands and the test goes green.
options.how: Re-point the test to allow only `merge --ready` (still refuse merge.py, --confirm and a bare Bash(merge)), red then green, and record your chat ask in a decision. Recommended only if you did ask for it in chat.
options.label: Keep the allow rule and re-point the test
options.lose: Any local session may run `merge --ready` with no prompt, while .claude/CLAUDE.md:31-32 says only the batch runner marks a PR ready.

options.gain: The test stays true and the batch-runner-only rule holds.
options.how: The two allow rules leave settings.json and the test stays as written.
options.label: Remove the allow rule
options.lose: Your chat ask is not honored; `merge --ready` prompts again.

shown.label: Keep the allow rule and re-point the test

title: Does the merge --ready allow rule in settings.json stay, or does the test that forbids it stand?
